_comment: Note 655's shape with synthetic names: two children in one exchange, a different observation about each. The transcript joins the two children in ONE clause, which note 655's own wording does not — its comma is removed on purpose, so the fixture tests the shared clause rather than a boundary the model can simply find. Green since #120: the prompt's span arithmetic carries an exception for this shape, the model returns a span per child at the same start, and AssembleNotes derives each span's end from the next greater start, so two spans hold the one clause with a summary each. Measured 25 runs of 25 on mistral-medium-2508 and 21 of 25 on gpt-5.4-mini; without the exception gpt-5.4-mini scored 0 of 25. This fixture is the guard on that sentence: it goes red if a model merges the clause into one span with both labels, which gives each child the other's observation (the #99 bleed), and red again if Go goes back to rejecting a repeated start, which fails the whole job. Nadia and Bruno are far apart phonetically on purpose: the only thing this fixture can fail on is the merge, never name resolution. The 'colours' clause is class-wide and reaches both children.
